paragraphs: Here's what I see, friend. Genesis spends a whole list on men who had sons and lived long lives, and then it stops on one line about Sarai: "But Sarai was barren; she had no children." (Genesis 11:30). Then the LORD speaks to Abram and promises, "I will make you into a great nation…" (Genesis 12:2). That's the LORD making a promise right where there's nothing to build on.

The second thing is that Abram goes. The LORD says, "Leave your country, your kindred, and your father's household, and go to the land I will show you." (Genesis 12:1). Abram departed "as the LORD had directed him" (Genesis 12:4), and he built an altar and called on the name of the LORD along the way (Genesis 12:7-8). He didn't get the whole map first. He got the LORD's word, and he walked on it.

And the promise is bigger than Abram. The LORD says "all the families of the earth will be blessed through you" (Genesis 12:3), so this isn't only about one family getting a good deal. So here's your takeaway, baker: when the LORD speaks, you can trust His word more than what you can see. I once had to trust a call out of a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, it holds up! This story isn't over, and the road has a whole lot more miles in it.
